brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at axial (-1,0,0), (0,0,0), (1,0,0), in a straight row, joined to each other; two joint bolts locked the joints; open faces capped.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: A 'Bin, full depth, drained' (hex-bin-full-drain) sits in each of the three cells; soil filled in each bin.
basil-young in the west cell, parsley-young in the centre, chives-young in the east; check_build clean, meshClash clear, no prop warnings.

requirements.requirement: Material suitability for wet/outdoor use (waterproofing, food safety, UV)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only; material choice is the user's and was not assessed.

finish.summary: Built a row of three full hex bases with a full-depth drained bin in each cell, capped open faces, locked joints, and planted basil, parsley and chives in soil. check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
